h1:
Breakfast Like a Lamphun Local
Before the Temple and Old Town
intro: Lamphun is a small town that's easy to explore on foot, and one of its quiet pleasures is breakfast. The old town around Wat Phra That Hariphunchai wakes up early, with fragrant coconut-milk khao soi, orange-hued khanom jeen nam ngiao that's mellow and balanced, coffee in old buildings, and a morning market where locals stop before starting the day. We've put it together as a breakfast plan that flows straight into a temple visit and an old-town walk all within walking distance.

blocks.html: Most people come to Lamphun to pay respects at Wat Phra That Hariphunchai, but if you get up a little earlier you'll catch something many visitors miss: a proper northern-style breakfast. Around the old town there are khao soi and khanom jeen nam ngiao shops that open early, coffee in old wooden buildings, and a morning market that's still busy. All of it sits within walking distance or a few minutes' drive, so you can eat and then walk straight into the temple.

blocks.text: Khao Soi & Nam Ngiao: the heart of a Lamphun morning

blocks.html: If you had to pick the two breakfast dishes that really stand for Lamphun, locals think of these first: khao soi, with its coconut-milk broth and northern curry paste, and khanom jeen nam ngiao (northerners call it khanom sen nam ngiao). The orange-tinted broth gets its color from dried red kapok flowers, with a gentle sourness and a rounded, balanced taste, eaten with crispy pork rind and fresh vegetables. These two bowls are the breakfast that teaches you what northern, Lamphun-style flavor is all about.

items.name: Khao Soi Sai Nam Phueng (Khao Soi Lamphun)
items.blurb: The khao soi shop Lamphun locals mention most often. The place is cute and well decorated, the broth is rich and aromatic, and you can choose chicken, beef or ribs. There are sweet add-ons like milk ice cream and matcha, making it an easy, relaxed way to start the morning.
items.meta: Mueang Lamphun district · open morning to afternoon

items.name: Khao Soi Jao Kao (across from Wat Phra That Hariphunchai)
items.blurb: An old shop right opposite Wat Phra That, with the best location if you plan to eat breakfast and walk straight into the temple. It serves chicken, beef and pork khao soi plus a meatball-only bowl, all at friendly prices.

items.name: Khanom Jeen Pa Sai
items.blurb: An old khanom jeen nam ngiao spot in a lane behind the former police station in town. It's a low-key place locals keep to themselves, with mellow, deeply savory nam ngiao and all the trimmings, perfect if you want a genuinely homestyle taste.
items.meta: In town, behind the old police station

items.name: Khanom Sen Mo Din (More Din Cafe)
items.blurb: A khanom jeen nam ngiao shop in true Lamphun style with a shady little garden and comfortable seating. The nam ngiao is fragrant with spices and just the right amount of punch, great if you want to eat khanom jeen in a relaxed cafe setting.

items.name: Baan Khanom Jeen Nam Ngiao Ob Mo Din
items.blurb: A khanom jeen nam ngiao shop in town that gets good reviews on travel sites. The clay-pot-baked nam ngiao is aromatic and well balanced, a solid backup if Pa Sai has a long queue.

items.name: Khao Soi Baan Yong
items.blurb: A long-running northern restaurant that focuses on khao soi, with a rich broth and a choice of beef or chicken. Prices start low, making it a good pick if you want homestyle khao soi without fussing over the atmosphere.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: The well-known khao soi and nam ngiao shops in Lamphun often sell out before afternoon. If there's a place you've got your eye on, aim to arrive before 11am to be safe. Many shops also close on certain weekdays, so check their day off before you head out from your accommodation.

blocks.text: Warm, comforting breakfasts: kai krata, rice soup, kuay jub

blocks.html: If you don't feel like starting the day with something bold and spicy, Lamphun also has warm, comforting Thai-style breakfasts: kai krata (eggs in a hot pan), rice soup, pa tong go (Thai crullers) and Vietnamese kuay jub. Many of these are old recipes from shops that have been around for years, the kind of place where you can sit in the morning sun before you head out.

items.name: Baan Tia
items.blurb: A breakfast shop with a 90s-era recipe, serving kai krata, soft-boiled eggs and pa tong go in a warm, old-fashioned set. Great if you like the feel of a traditional morning spot.

items.name: Sawasdee Yam Chao
items.blurb: A chic breakfast spot in town with rice soup, kai krata, steamed bread and soft-boiled eggs, served with coffee. Comfortable for sitting through the morning into late morning.

items.name: Vietnamese Kuay Jub Breakfast Shop
items.blurb: Another local breakfast favorite: Vietnamese kuay jub with a clear broth packed with toppings, eaten with bread or soft-boiled eggs. A light way to start the day without filling up.

blocks.text: Morning coffee in the old town, around the temple

blocks.html: Part of Lamphun's charm is that many cafes sit inside old wooden buildings and traditional houses around Wat Phra That Hariphunchai, just a few minutes' walk from the temple. Several open by 7–8am, perfect if you want a coffee before going in. Lamphun is also longan country, so you'll find an unusual option to try: longan coffee.

items.name: Black to Basic
items.blurb: A loft-style cafe in black and white, open and airy, on the same street as Wat Phra That. It opens at 7am, ideal for a coffee before you walk into the temple.

items.name: Temple House Lamphun
items.blurb: A cafe in an old house in the middle of the old town, right across from Wat Phra That. It looks out on the temple wall with a quiet atmosphere, and opens early through to evening (closed Tuesdays).

items.name: Yann Slowbar
items.blurb: A second-floor slow-bar cafe in a vintage old building on Inthayongyot Road. Drip-coffee fans will love it, and there's bakery to go with it (it opens a little later, so it suits a late-morning breakfast).

items.name: Hhom Cafe
items.blurb: A minimalist cafe showcasing local craft work, with a small garden out front and a quiet, easy atmosphere, a few minutes' walk from Wat Phra That (closed Mondays).

blocks.html: Lamphun's old town is small and traffic is light, so park near Wat Phra That, then pay your respects and follow it up with coffee easily. Most of these shops are within a 5–10 minute walk of the temple.

If you want to see what a real Lamphun morning looks like, the market is the answer. You'll find ready-to-eat food, fresh produce, seasonal longan, and local souvenirs. It's a pleasant wander that gives you the feel of a small town, snacking as you go before heading to the temple.

items: Nong Dok Market (Kad Nong Dok) — Lamphun's big, popular market near the Queen Chamadevi monument, with both food and household goods, and several of Lamphun's legendary old shops.
Ready-to-eat morning bites — sticky rice with sai ua (northern sausage), crispy pork rind, nam prik num and local sweets, all easy to grab and snack on as you walk.
Lamphun souvenirs — longan and longan products like longan cake, longan cookies and dried longan, the souvenirs most tied to this town.

blocks.text: A morning plan before the temple and old town

blocks.html: Here's an unhurried morning plan: eat well, sip a coffee, then visit the temple and walk the old town, all within walking distance. It works for both day-trippers and people staying overnight in Lamphun, and you can go the khao soi route or the nam ngiao route.

items.activity: Start the morning with a popular khao soi
items.note: Khao Soi Sai Nam Phueng, or Khao Soi Jao Kao across from the temple if you want to walk straight in afterward.
Lamphun's landmark temple. Walk around the golden chedi and the Lanna-style viharn.
Black to Basic or Temple House across from the temple, a good spot to rest and soak up the atmosphere.
Walk along Inthayongyot Road to see the old wooden houses and craft shops before splitting off to explore more.
Watch Lamphun's morning life and pick up longan souvenirs and ready-to-eat bites.

items.activity: Nam ngiao at an old shop
items.note: Khanom Jeen Pa Sai or Khanom Sen Mo Din for that homestyle northern flavor.
Hhom Cafe, or Yann Slowbar if you're running late, for a sip before the temple.
Cap off the morning at Wat Phra That Hariphunchai and walk the town, all within easy reach.

faq.q: What's a good local breakfast in Lamphun?
faq.a: The two dishes locals think of first are khao soi, with its coconut-milk broth and northern curry paste, and khanom jeen nam ngiao (khanom sen nam ngiao), the orange, mellow-tasting noodle soup. If you want something lighter, there's also kai krata (eggs in a hot pan), rice soup, and Vietnamese kuay jub at breakfast shops around town.

faq.q: Where can I eat khao soi near Wat Phra That Hariphunchai?
faq.a: Khao Soi Jao Kao sits right opposite Wat Phra That Hariphunchai, ideal if you want to eat breakfast and walk straight into the temple. Khao Soi Sai Nam Phueng is a popular shop in town that Lamphun locals mention often, with a rich broth and comfortable seating.

faq.q: Do old-town cafes in Lamphun open early?
faq.a: Yes. Several cafes around Wat Phra That open by 7–8am, such as Black to Basic (07:00) and Temple House (07:00), just a few minutes' walk from the temple, perfect for a coffee before you go in. Slow-bar spots like Yann open later (around 10am).

faq.q: Which morning market should I go to in Lamphun?
faq.a: Nong Dok Market (Kad Nong Dok) near the Queen Chamadevi monument is the big, popular one, with ready-to-eat food, fresh produce and longan souvenirs. It's a pleasant place to watch Lamphun's morning life.

faq.q: What snack souvenirs can I buy from Lamphun?
faq.a: Lamphun is longan country, so the souvenirs revolve around longan: longan cake, longan cookies and dried longan. You'll also find northern bites like crispy pork rind and sai ua (northern sausage) to take home at the markets.
